description: General gastroenterology new consult. Iron deficiency anaemia workup with explicit GP action (colonoscopy referral). Clear medication dose. Completed investigation (gastroscopy). Tests: required facts recall, explicit GP action detection, completed vs planned investigation distinction.
transcript:
Gastroenterologist: Good morning, Mr Hartley. I've had a look at the referral from Dr Nguyen. You're here today regarding iron deficiency anaemia that was picked up on routine bloods.

Patient: That's right. I felt a bit run down and my GP ordered some bloods. They came back showing low iron.

Gastroenterologist: Your ferritin was 6 micrograms per litre and haemoglobin 102. The gastroscopy that you had last month at St Andrew's was reported as normal — no coeliac changes, no ulcers, no oesophagitis. So the upper GI tract is clear. Have you had any change in bowel habit, rectal bleeding, or weight loss?

Patient: No bleeding that I've noticed. Bowel habit has been a bit slower than usual over the last three or four months, but no blood.

Gastroenterologist: That change in bowel habit in the context of iron deficiency is something we need to investigate. You're 58 and you haven't had a colonoscopy. Given these findings I'd like to organise a colonoscopy to exclude a colonic lesion as the source of iron depletion. I'll write to Dr Nguyen with the plan.

Patient: That sounds reasonable. Do I need any iron tablets in the meantime?

Gastroenterologist: Yes, I'll recommend that Dr Nguyen commence iron supplementation — ferrous sulfate 325 milligrams once daily with meals — while we wait for the colonoscopy. The change in bowel habit over three to four months together with iron deficiency means the colonoscopy is the priority.
